title: Cell-level DEG plan
task: Compare subtype 2 vs subtype 1 within tumor macrophages.
context: Six patients per subtype; cell yield varies ten-fold.

steps.text: Pool all macrophages by subtype.
steps.issue: Removes patient-level replication and hides heterogeneity.

steps.text: Run cell-level Wilcoxon FindMarkers.
steps.issue: Pseudoreplication for a patient-level subtype contrast.

steps.text: Keep genes with raw P<0.05.
steps.issue: No multiple-testing control or effect threshold.

steps.text: Run KEGG on significant genes.
steps.issue: Only interpretable after a valid DEG result and explicit universe/direction.

steps.text: Claim subtype-specific macrophage biology.
steps.issue: Confounding and patient consistency are unaddressed.

seniorSummary: The plan's central error is using cells as independent replicates. Rebuild the contrast at patient×cell-type level and retain subject covariates.
transferPrompt: Write the aggregation key and design formula for your analogous comparison.

title: Survival model plan
task: Test whether a protein predicts overall survival.

steps.text: Dichotomize every continuous variable at its median.
steps.issue: Information loss and arbitrary cutpoints.

steps.text: Run univariable Cox models and retain P<0.05 variables.
steps.issue: Data-driven screening omits confounder/prognostic rationale and adds instability.

steps.text: Fit the retained variables plus protein in one Cox model.
steps.issue: 31 events may not support the effective complexity; penalization/pre-specification needed.

steps.text: Check proportional hazards and nonlinear functional form.
Report adjusted HR and confidence interval.

seniorSummary: The AI selected variables and transformations from the same sparse outcome data. The adjusted HR would likely be unstable.
transferPrompt: Count events and effective parameters in your planned survival model.

title: Model validation plan
task: Validate a recurrence model developed at center A.
context: Center B has 260 patients and 70 events.

steps.text: Refit all coefficients in center B.
steps.issue: This prevents untouched validation of the original model.

steps.text: Select a new optimal risk threshold in center B.
steps.issue: Uses validation outcomes to tune the decision rule.

steps.text: Report C-index only.
steps.issue: Absolute-risk calibration and clinical utility are missing.

steps.text: Apply the full locked model and preprocessing first.
Report calibration intercept, slope, plot, and discrimination.

seniorSummary: Untouched application must precede any recalibration or model updating.
transferPrompt: List the exact model objects that must remain locked in your external validation.

title: Cell proportion plan
task: Compare regulatory T-cell abundance between responders and nonresponders.
context: Five versus five patients with unequal capture depth.

steps.text: Pool all cells within response groups.
steps.issue: Destroys patient-level variation.

steps.text: Apply chi-square test to pooled counts.
steps.issue: Cells are not independent and composition is ignored.

steps.text: Plot each patient's proportion and total captured cells.
Use a sample-aware abundance/compositional model.
Interpret captured fraction as absolute tissue abundance.
steps.issue: Dissociation and sampling affect capture proportions.

seniorSummary: The inferential unit is patient; pooled-cell significance cannot establish response-group abundance.
transferPrompt: Create a per-patient abundance plot for one cell class in your project.

title: Spatial mechanism plan
task: Test whether macrophages drive exhausted T-cell niches.
context: Three tumors; spot-based transcriptomics and matched histology.

steps.text: Compute spot-level ligand–receptor scores.
steps.issue: Useful hypothesis generation, but resolution and mixture must be explicit.

steps.text: Pool spots and test adjacency as independent observations.
steps.issue: Patient/section nesting is ignored.

steps.text: Adjust for tissue compartment and local density.
Validate proximity with multiplex imaging.
Conclude causal macrophage signaling.
steps.issue: Proximity/expression lacks direction and perturbation.

seniorSummary: The data can establish spatial association, not a causal interaction. Mechanism needs molecular and functional intervention.
transferPrompt: Name one anatomical confounder and one perturbation for your spatial hypothesis.

title: Pathway enrichment plan

steps.text: Use paired patient design for gene-level statistics.
Select raw P<0.05 genes.
steps.issue: Multiplicity is ignored.

steps.text: Use every known human gene as ORA background.
steps.issue: Background should reflect genes eligible/tested in the assay.

steps.text: Run signed ranked enrichment with FDR.
Call enriched pathways activated mechanisms.
steps.issue: Expression enrichment is not pathway activity or causality.

seniorSummary: A valid paired gene-level statistic and explicit enrichment universe are prerequisites; interpret pathways as programs, not mechanisms.
transferPrompt: Record the gene universe and ranking statistic for your next enrichment run.

title: Clustering plan
task: Discover proteomic subtypes associated with survival.

steps.text: Normalize and examine batch–clinical balance.
Try k=2…10 and choose the smallest survival P value.
steps.issue: Outcome-guided cluster selection causes double dipping.

steps.text: Check resampling stability and batch composition.
Describe pathways distinguishing the selected clusters.
steps.issue: Descriptive only until selection and enrichment are valid.

steps.text: Call the clusters validated clinical subtypes.
steps.issue: No locked classifier or independent cohort.

seniorSummary: Choose and validate structure independently of the same outcome test; external assignment is needed for a subtype claim.
transferPrompt: Choose two perturbations under which your subtype solution should remain stable.

title: Multi-omics integration plan
context: Matched RNA, protein, and methylation in 48 patients.

steps.text: Filter features using response labels in all patients.
steps.issue: Supervised selection leaks outcomes into evaluation.

steps.text: Concatenate z-scored modalities.
steps.issue: A baseline is possible but weights, missingness, and scale assumptions need justification.

steps.text: Randomly split omic rows rather than patients.
steps.issue: Patient identity must define the split.

steps.text: Nest integration, selection, and tuning inside patient-level CV.
Compare against modality-specific and clinical baselines.

seniorSummary: The full integration procedure—not only the last classifier—must be evaluated within patient-level resampling.
transferPrompt: Draw your integration and model-selection operations inside an outer patient split.

title: Biomarker plan
task: Develop an IHC marker for recurrence risk.
context: Discovery tissue microarray and a second core from the same patients.

steps.text: Optimize staining cutoff against recurrence.
steps.issue: Permissible discovery, but must be labeled and locked before validation.

steps.text: Use the second core from the same patients as external validation.
steps.issue: This is technical/spatial replication, not independent clinical validation.

steps.text: Report inter-reader and assay reproducibility.
Adjust for established clinical prognostic factors.
Claim the marker is ready for clinical use.
steps.issue: External validity and utility are absent.

seniorSummary: Analytical replication and independent clinical validation answer different questions and must not be conflated.
transferPrompt: Separate your biomarker evidence into analytical validity, clinical validity, and utility.

title: Organoid drug plan
task: Test a targeted drug in patient-derived organoids.
context: Two donor lines; eight wells per dose.

steps.text: Treat every well as an independent n.
steps.issue: Wells are nested technical observations.

steps.text: Fit dose-response curves per donor.
Report target engagement and normal-cell selectivity.
Use the concentration with maximal effect without exposure context.
steps.issue: Clinical plausibility and dose selection are unaddressed.

steps.text: Claim likely patient efficacy.
steps.issue: Two in vitro donors do not establish clinical benefit.

seniorSummary: Evidence supports responses in tested organoids only; donor-level replication, pharmacology, and in vivo/clinical triangulation are missing.
transferPrompt: State your biological replicate and clinically plausible exposure range.

title: Causal language plan
task: Draft a narrative from cross-sectional tumor profiling.
context: Expression, survival association, and pathway enrichment only.

steps.text: Say the factor is associated with poor survival.
Say the factor drives metastasis.
steps.issue: No perturbation, temporality, or causal identification.

steps.text: Say enriched programs are compatible with EMT biology.
Say pathway analysis proves EMT activation.
steps.issue: Enrichment is annotation-level expression evidence.

steps.text: Propose perturbation and rescue as next experiments.

seniorSummary: Calibrate verbs to evidence: association and program compatibility are supported; mechanistic driving is not.
transferPrompt: Audit the causal verbs in one current figure title.

title: Figure narrative plan
task: Organize a paper on a candidate immune target.
context: Data include cohort association, scRNA localization, spatial proximity, cell-line knockdown, and mouse response.

steps.text: Open with cohort/question and discovery.
Place localization before claiming a cell-specific mechanism.
Present spatial proximity as functional validation.
steps.issue: Spatial association does not validate function.

steps.text: Use perturbation then in vivo response to climb the evidence ladder.
End with clinical efficacy as established.
steps.issue: Mouse efficacy is not clinical efficacy.

seniorSummary: The narrative should make each figure perform one evidence task and keep the terminal claim at preclinical support.
transferPrompt: Label the evidence job of each figure in your draft with one verb phrase.

title: Literature citation plan
task: Support a method choice using an AI-generated reading list.
context: The AI supplies 12 DOI/PMID pairs without quotations or metadata checks.

steps.text: Save all citations as verified because identifiers look plausible.
steps.issue: Plausible identifiers can be fabricated or mismatched.

steps.text: Resolve identifiers through PubMed/Crossref.
Check that each source supports the exact claim.
Keep unresolved items pending while offline.
Let AI-generated explanation overwrite user notes.
steps.issue: Original user work and generated content must remain separate.

seniorSummary: Metadata resolution is necessary but not sufficient: claim-level support must also be inspected, and generated content remains distinct.
transferPrompt: Choose one citation in your project and record identifier, source type, supported claim, and verification date.

title: Data leakage plan
context: Three slides and multiple tiles per patient; 130 patients.

steps.text: Normalize all slides before splitting.
steps.issue: Fixed normalization may be acceptable; learned normalization must be trained within folds.

steps.text: Randomly split image tiles into folds.
steps.issue: Tiles from one patient leak identity across folds.

steps.text: Select genes using all survival outcomes.
steps.issue: Outcome-aware feature leakage.

steps.text: Group outer folds by patient and nest selection/tuning.
Evaluate calibration in addition to discrimination.

seniorSummary: Split by the highest independent unit before every learned operation; tiles and slides cannot cross patient folds.
transferPrompt: Identify the highest grouping unit for every modality in your prediction pipeline.

title: External reference plan
task: Validate an AI-generated risk score in a public cohort.
context: The formula omits preprocessing details and uses unavailable variables.

steps.text: Impute unavailable predictors as zero.
steps.issue: Changes the model without justification and can create systematic error.

steps.text: Infer preprocessing from the validation data.
steps.issue: The original model is not reproducible/locked.

steps.text: Request the full formula, coding, baseline risk, and preprocessing.
Document target-cohort differences and missingness.
If unrecoverable, label validation infeasible rather than fabricate implementation.

seniorSummary: A model that cannot be fully implemented cannot be externally validated. Transparency is a methodological prerequisite, not an administrative detail.
transferPrompt: List every artifact another center needs to reproduce your model predictions.
